abstract: Monitors redundant emergency satellite uplinks and data telemetry latency for maritime tracking
system_message:
You are the Telecommunications officer (TEL), responsible for monitoring redundant emergency satellite uplinks and evaluating data telemetry latency for maritime tracking.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: VHF emergency channel monitoring（FREQ）
information_points.content:
TEL-FREQ-MZ9：For the Specialized offshore support vessel convoy plan, transceiver testing on the Channel 16 maritime distress band registers a VHF marine signal-to-noise ratio of 24 dB during adverse atmospheric conditions.
TEL-FREQ-QWK：Diagnostic logs for the Helicopter airlift and standby cutter plan demonstrate a VHF marine signal-to-noise ratio of 30 dB across the Channel 16 maritime distress band under adverse atmospheric test conditions.
TEL-FREQ-LCE：Emergency transceiver diagnostic logs for the Heavy-lift multi-catamaran flotilla plan reflect a VHF marine signal-to-noise ratio of 18 dB on the Channel 16 maritime distress band during adverse atmospheric testing.

information_points.title: Monitors redundant emergency satellite uplinks and data telemetry latency for maritime tracking（COMS）
information_points.content:
TEL-COMS-RDM：For the Heavy-lift multi-catamaran flotilla plan, the primary geostationary emergency transceivers show that an active satellite telemetry uplink is operational between the evacuation unit and mission control, with a round-trip telemetry latency of 80 ms recorded across a 15-minute continuous test packet stream.
TEL-COMS-5GY：For the Specialized offshore support vessel convoy plan, the active satellite telemetry uplink is operational across primary geostationary transceivers, and the round-trip telemetry latency over the active link is 80 ms during the 15-minute benchmark stream.
TEL-COMS-OE2：Under the Helicopter airlift and standby cutter plan, an active satellite telemetry uplink is confirmed operational via the primary geostationary emergency transceivers, while diagnostic testing indicates a round-trip telemetry latency of 180 ms across the continuous test packet stream.
